business_scope.primary_industry_name: Precision CO2 Laser Cutting of 3D Mechanical Wooden Puzzles

Convention between France and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1995, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 et seq.; Code de commerce, Articles L.233-3, L.233-4, L.561-45 and R.561-1 et seq.; Décret n° 2017-1094 du 12 juin 2017 relatif au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Sapin II) on transparency, anti-corruption and modernisation of economic life.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (not available for general public search; accessible only to TRACFIN, judicial authorities and obliged entities carrying out AML/CFT due diligence under applicable legal conditions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport or national identity card of each ultimate beneficial owner and controlling shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registry or passport authority of the relevant jurisdiction; for French owners, the Préfecture or competent consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued by a Contracting State; consular legalization for non-Hague countries; certified translation into French by a sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, excerpt and good standing certificate of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation (e.g., Greffe du Tribunal de commerce in France, Companies Registry abroad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO register extract / beneficial ownership declaration of each direct corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry in which the direct shareholder is registered (French Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs or corresponding foreign statutory register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of tax residence for each shareholder or UBO contributing capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Tax administration of the residence country (DGFiP in France or competent foreign revenue authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified French translation; acceptable only if issued within the last 90 days

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Domiciliation agreement or lease for the proposed registered office of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed corporate domiciliation company or landlord of the industrial/commercial premises
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed outside France, notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization and sworn French translation; if executed in France, original lease or domiciliation certificate without apostille is sufficient

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, statutory representatives, directors and persons acting on behalf of the company against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Council consolidated financial sanctions database (EUSANCTION), the French national asset-freeze list maintained by the DG Trésor, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List. Politically Exposed Persons are identified and assessed in accordance with French Code monétaire et financier Articles L.561-10-2, R.561-18-1 and the EU AML/CFT Directives. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs, including source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval. AML/CFT records must be retained for at least five years after the termination of business relations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); name availability verification through Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr) and INPI trademark database (data.inpi.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 du 10 août 1994) and Article L.121-1 of the French Consumer Code, the corporate name must be in French or in Latin-script transliteration from non-Latin writing systems. The legal form suffix 'SAS' must be included in the name. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public order, or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name or protected trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Crédit / Caisse (regulated banking terms requiring prior authorisation from the ACPR)
Assurance / Mutuelle / Réassurance (terms reserved to regulated insurance and mutual entities)
Société de gestion / Gestion de portefeuille / AMF (regulatory titles implying AMF authorisation)
Fiduciaire / Trust / Trustee (terms requiring specific fiduciary authorisation or reserve)
République / État / National / Ministère / Officiel (terms implying governmental or public-official character)
Pharmacie / Officine / Laboratoire pharmaceutique (regulated pharmacy or health terms)
Avocat / Notaire / Huissier / Conseil juridique (terms reserved to regulated legal professions)
Fondation / Fondation d'utilité publique (requires official recognition)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the RCS registrar or the Guichet unique rejects the proposed corporate name, the applicant’s legal counsel must submit a written rectification and resubmission within 30 days of the rejection notice, amending Article 2 of the draft articles to propose an alternative available name. If the registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an urgent injunction application (référé) before the Tribunal de commerce, requesting the registrar to proceed with registration, pursuant to Code de commerce Articles L.123-5-1 and R.123-11, and may also challenge the underlying trademark conflict at the INPI. No separate administrative extension is available for name reservation; however, an INPI trademark filing preserves priority for 10 years once accepted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office is not permissible for an SAS engaged in physical assembly and production of laser-cut wooden puzzles. France requires a genuine registered office (siège social) and, where production is performed, a physical establishment (établissement) with adequate space, power supply, ventilation and fire-safety compliance. A third-party corporate domiciliation company may lawfully serve as the administrative registered office at formation, but the actual production premises must be distinctly declared and leased; here, virtual-office-only registration would be rejected under commercial-substance and tax-residence principles.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; quantified annualised risk of unannounced on-site inspection in the first operating year is estimated at 20%. Competent authorities include DGFiP tax inspectors, URSSAF labour and social-security inspectors, DRIEETS labour authorities, and DGCCRF product-safety inspectors, with particular attention to EN 71 toy-safety compliance and fire safety pertaining to laser cutting.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation agreement, first quarter advance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed corporate domiciliation company or commercial landlord

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Agreed fixed fee or professional hourly rate; market benchmark for a simple SAS ranges from USD 1,000 to USD 2,500

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-2, L.210-6, L.227-1 to L.227-19, L.227-9, R.227-1; related provisions of the Monetary and Financial Code for blocked capital; INPI Guichet Unique implementing decree.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, transmitting to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (articles of association) and the standard application for RCS registration filed electronically through the INPI Guichet Unique; final corporate existence evidenced by Extrait Kbis
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS. Cash subscriptions must be released in at least 50% at subscription, with the balance paid within five years; the released funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account with a bank, Caisse des Dépôts, or notary until RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the shareholders of [Company] SAS, in accordance with the French Commercial Code, that: (1) the attached Articles of Association are approved and the share subscriptions listed therein are ratified; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address]; (3) [Name] is appointed first President, with full management powers under the Articles; (4) the President is authorized to complete RCS registration through the Guichet Unique, sign declarations, open bank accounts and appoint advisors; (5) the President is directed to procure all industrial, environmental and fire-safety authorizations required for the laser-cutting workshop; and (6) all incorporation expenses and liabilities incurred before registration are ratified and treated as company expenses. This resolution is effective upon issuance of the Kbis extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability and Trademark Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI data portal and Infogreffe online databases
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the French company register and INPI trademark database to confirm that the proposed SAS name is available and not confusingly similar to an existing right. Confirm the preferred domain name and determine if any preliminary trademark registration is advisable. French law does not offer a formal name reservation; protection is perfected at RCS registration and through INPI trademark filing.
required_dossiers: Two or three proposed corporate names
Trademark and domain name availability check
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is identical or confusingly similar, select the next available variant and use that variant consistently in the articles and all filing documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders; French notary if real property or special in-kind contributions are made
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS statutes in accordance with the intended corporate purpose: precision CO2 laser cutting, assembly, packaging, and sale of wooden mechanical puzzles. Set the registered office, duration (generally 99 years), share capital, share classes, presidency and collective decision-making rules. Have all shareholders sign the statutes in original or electronic signature format. Notarize the statutes if real estate or a business undertaking is contributed.
required_dossiers: Identity and legal capacity documents of all shareholders
Valuation report for any in-kind contribution
Written consent of the proposed President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary or registry officer identifies an unlawful or ambiguous clause, adopt a shareholder resolution amending or deleting the clause before the RCS filing is submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Escrow and Deposit of Cash Subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French regulated bank, Caisse des Dépôts, or French notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporarily blocked company formation account in the intended corporate name. Deposit at least 50% of each cash subscription and obtain an attestation de blocage de fonds from the bank or escrow agent. The funds are released automatically or upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Schedule of subscribers and paid cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further anti-money-laundering information, supply shareholder passports, source-of-funds evidence and corporate structure statements; if the certificate contains a typographical error, request reissuance before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Legal Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) approved for the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal notice to a licensed legal announcements journal stating the corporate form 'Société par Actions Simplifiée', corporate name, registered office, share capital, corporate purpose, duration and first President. The notice must appear before or on the date of the RCS filing; obtain the publisher's certificate of publication.
required_dossiers: Blocked capital certificate if referenced in the notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is rejected for inconsistency, correct the text to match the articles and republish; the publication certificate generally remains valid for three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing with INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in and complete the 'Création d'une société par actions simplifiée' application. Upload the signed articles, blocked-fund certificate, JAL publication certificate, proof of registered-office occupation, identity documents, beneficial-owner declaration and powers of attorney. Pay the official filing fee electronically and submit the complete dossier. INPI performs formal control and forwards the dossier to the competent court registry.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office occupation and landlord consent
Identity and residence proof for shareholders and President
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INPI issues an incompleteness notice or evidence request, submit the missing documents within fifteen calendar days. If the dossier is rejected for substantive inconsistency, correct the statutes by shareholder resolution and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The court registry reviews the legal conformity of the dossier, verifies the President's mandate and shareholder identity, and enrolls the SAS in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés. INSEE attributes SIREN and SIRET numbers, and the registry issues the Kbis extract, which constitutes official proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: INPI filing acknowledgment and dossier reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is refused, obtain the written rejection, remedy the cited defect by a corrective shareholder resolution or supplementary declaration, and resubmit; a refusal may also be challenged before the competent Court of Appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Employer and Insurance Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, URSSAF, DREETS/DREET, Service des Impôts des Entreprises, and CNIL where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the SIREN/SIRET identifiers, register as an employer with URSSAF, register for VAT and business taxes, and complete CNIL data-protection obligations if customer or employee data are processed. Subscribe civil liability, property, and fire insurance covering the laser-cutting workshop and finished-goods inventory.
required_dossiers: Civil liability and fire insurance certificates
Data processing register and CNIL compliance file if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INSEE or URSSAF shows a data mismatch, reconcile using the Kbis extract and submit a rectification request; if employer registration is delayed, use the spontaneous declaration procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupancy, Zoning and Pre-Licensing Physical Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mairie / Préfecture and qualified building or electrical safety engineers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the intended premises are zoned for light industrial or workshop use and obtain a zoning certificate or planning non-opposition if required. Confirm structural floor-load capacity and three-phase electrical supply for the CO2 laser cutter. If the lease requires it, notify the landlord of the industrial use and obtain written consent.
required_dossiers: Zoning certificate or planning search result
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning prohibits manufacturing, relocate to a compliant premise or apply for a planning adjustment; if the power supply or floor load is insufficient, arrange an electrical upgrade or reinforcement before installation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) – Inspection des Installations Classées; Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS); Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate sectoral operating licence is required for wooden-puzzle manufacturing; the mandatory physical and environmental clearances are the ICPE declaration receipt (récépissé de déclaration) for the laser woodworking activity and the municipal fire-safety certification, together with workplace occupational-health clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique – DREAL / Inspection des Installations Classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE 'Déclaration' (DC) regime for a small-scale wood laser-cutting and assembly workshop under the applicable wood-processing and combustion-related nomenclature, typically Rubrique 2354; no full environmental impact assessment is required below the 'Enregistrement' or 'Autorisation' thresholds. If production capacity or wood storage exceeds the relevant thresholds, the project is reclassified to 'Enregistrement' with an environmental baseline statement and public consultation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater shall be discharged to the municipal sewer without prior non-domestic discharge approval; ventilation and dust-extraction systems must maintain airborne wood-dust concentrations below the applicable French occupational exposure limit (VLEP-8h, currently 3.6 mg/m³ for inhalable wood dust); laser-generated fumes and VOCs must be filtered with HEPA or activated-carbon filtration where visible emissions, odour or VOC thresholds are exceeded; sawdust and offcuts must be stored in non-combustible containers and disposed of under CER waste codes 03 01 01 or 03 01 05; noise emissions must not exceed the emergence limits stated in the relevant ICPE operational order.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain an SDIS fire-safety inspection and certificate of fire-safety compliance, including smoke detection, extinguishers, evacuation signage and a laser-equipment interlock; obtain a structural load inspection and electrical conformity certificate confirming the floor and power supply are suitable for the laser cutter; prepare and maintain a Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), appoint a laser-safety officer, use Class 1 enclosures or equivalent guarding, and complete the DREETS workplace registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) under the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty. Official taxpayer portal: www.impots.gouv.fr. Company formation, SIREN/SIRET allocation and TIN delivery are coordinated via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The French SAS is incorporated electronically through the Guichet Unique, which transmits the dossier to the commercial court registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce), INSEE for SIREN (9 digits) and SIRET (14 digits), and DGFiP for tax registration. Once INSEE validates the registration, DGFiP issues the French VAT number (TVA intracommunautaire: FR + 11 digits) in accordance with CGI Article 286-ter, without any separate application for established French entities. A non-EU foreign entity carrying out taxable supplies in France (e.g., selling goods held in a French FBA warehouse) must file the non-resident VAT registration form (Cerfa n° 14945*06) with the DGFiP non-resident business tax office; when such entity has no establishment in the EU, a DGFiP-accredited fiscal representative (responsable solidaire) must be appointed and is jointly liable for the VAT under CGI Article 289-A, unless the OSS/IOSS scheme is electable for distance sales. Foreign entities acquiring French real estate or participating in French supply chains must also secure a separate French TIN where required for withholding or property taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SAS is unconditionally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS, CGI Art. 206(1)); there is no pass-through eligibility for shareholders. Ordinary corporate profits are taxed at the standard 25% corporate income tax rate from fiscal year 2024 onward. The French territorial scope taxes all profits arising from establishments and activities carried on in France, while profits derived from foreign permanent establishments are exempt provided they are subject to adequate taxation in the foreign State.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections for the SAS include: (i) election to form a fiscal integration group where a French-resident head company holds at least 95% of the SAS (CGI Art. 223-A), allowing a single group-wide IS computation; (ii) election to form a VAT single taxable person ('assujetti unique') group under CGI Art. 256-C; (iii) election to use the simplified real tax regime (régime réel simplifié) for small and medium businesses; (iv) option to make the SAS taxable as a group member under the parent-subsidiary participation exemption where applicable. Hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD transposition, CGI Art. 212-bis) apply mandatorily and cannot be waived by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Goods supplies within France: basic VAT exemption threshold (franchise en base) of €85,000 and upper threshold of €93,500 for 2025 (CGI Art. 293-B). Cross-border intra-Community distance sales to consumers of goods: €10,000 EU-wide annual threshold unless the OSS election is made. Sellers holding goods in France (e.g., Amazon FBA stock) are required to register for French VAT from the first Euro of French taxable turnover, as no turnover threshold applies to domestic stock-based sales. Exporters commonly register voluntarily to secure zero-rating on export transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing applies in France from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size taxpayers and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro businesses. Invoices must be issued in the structured EN 16931 / Factur-X (PEPPOL) format through an accredited PDP (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire) and transmitted to the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) DGFiP API. B2C transaction data are reportable electronically to the PPF. France does not impose real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping; verification is post-event and decentralised, with risk-based audits of e-invoice flows.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU are eligible for the 0% VAT rate (CGI Art. 262-I-1°) where the goods are physically dispatched outside the EU pursuant to a customs export declaration, transport documents, and the export contract. Intra-Community supplies to another EU taxable person are zero-rated under CGI Art. 262-ter provided the customer's EU VAT number is validated and the relevant EC Sales List is filed. Services directly linked to exported goods and services supplied to non-EU recipients without establishment in France may be zero-rated under CGI Arts. 259-A and 262-I-2°. For e-commerce FBA exports, the seller must retain the DAU/EEX customs acceptance and carrier evidence. France does not impose a formal statutory FX repatriation deadline; the system default of 180 days is used administratively as the documentary time window for proving receipt of export proceeds in audits and refund reviews.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/EEX) accepted by French Customs (DGDDI)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical exit from the EU
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export sales contract
Inward Remittance Certificate and SWIFT/bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
EU Sales List (EC Sales List) and Intrastat filings where applicable for intra-Community dispatches
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where 0% export VAT is claimed without sufficient documentary proof of physical export, DGFiP recharacterises the transaction as a taxable domestic supply and assesses 20% French VAT together with late-payment interest at 0.20% per month. Penalties escalate to 40% of the assessed tax for deliberate misconduct (manquement délibéré) under CGI Art. 1729 and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres; false or fictitious export invoices expose the taxpayer to the 50% specific penalty under Art. 1737. The ordinary assessment limitation is three years, extended to six years for concealed activity or tax fraud. Criminal prosecutions under CGI Art. 1741 may result in imprisonment up to five years and fines up to €500,000, plus mandatory clawback of previously refunded export VAT and suspension of advance-refund procedures until the audit is closed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under full capital and current account convertibility as an EU member state and IMF Article VIII currency. Euro-denominated transactions face no restrictions. Capital account items including profit repatriation, dividend distributions, and equity contributions are unrestricted subject only to standard corporate and tax compliance. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders encounter no convertibility hurdles beyond routine 12.8% withholding tax and automatic exchange of information reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds applies under French law. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency bank accounts without conversion. Companies must however file statistical declarations with the Banque de France for trade balance purposes and customs declarations for statistical reporting. No fixed timeline exists for surrender; voluntary FX conversion is available through banking channels at prevailing market rates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility rating for regulated electronic money institutions including Stripe and PayPal, both licensed as EMI under French and EU PSD2 frameworks. Legal constraints require full compliance with French AML/CFT obligations, beneficial ownership registration, and transaction monitoring; offshore digital EMIs serving French entities must maintain local licensing or partner with authorized French banks to avoid regulatory breaches.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding and KYC is fully permitted for French SAS entities through approved platforms. Directors may be required to complete video KYC interviews or appear in person for enhanced due diligence in cases involving complex ownership structures, high transaction volumes, or perceived risk indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified extract from Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) plus beneficial ownership declaration filed with French financial intelligence unit (TRACFIN)
Corporate bank statements, audited financial statements, tax returns, and detailed business plan demonstrating revenue from precision laser cutting of wooden puzzles
Comprehensive screening report plus supporting corporate documentation and director declarations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SEPA credit transfers for euro amounts or SWIFT MT103 for international wires. Purpose codes include 'CAP' for capital contributions and 'EQ' for equity injections. Verification requires matching beneficiary IBAN/SWIFT details against company RCS registration, shareholder resolutions, and supporting documentation including board minutes and valuation reports.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international payments or Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 rules. Intra-EU transactions may use SEPA Instant or standard SEPA transfers. All disbursements require proper commercial invoices, proof of goods receipt, and compliance with transfer pricing documentation where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return 'liasse fiscale' — Forms 2065-SD, 2056-SD, 2058-SD, 2059-SD and related annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) — Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SAS, the return must be filed by the second business day after 1 May; online filers generally receive an extended deadline to 15 May. Non-calendar-year entities follow the tax administration's electronic filing calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic penalty on assessed corporate income tax, increased to 40% for bad faith and 80% for fraudulent behavior, plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; prolonged non-filing permits tax administration to assess the corporate income tax ex officio and may lead to enforced collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts — balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, notes, management report, and auditor's report where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce via the INPI Guichet Unique for registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve annual accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end; filed annual accounts must be lodged with the registry within 1 month of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory window exposes the SAS to injunctive action before the President of the Commercial Court, compulsory payments ('astreintes'), criminal fines of up to EUR 15,000 for deliberate non-compliance, and risk of registry strike-off proceedings for failure to maintain valid registration information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration Sociale Nominative (DSN) — annual payroll and social security declaration transmitted monthly, including definitive annual payroll data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF and Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP) under the shared social-security reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly DSN due no later than the 5th or 15th of the month following the pay period; final annual closing data must be included in the first payroll declaration of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missed DSN filings subject the employer to flat late-payment penalties on contribution amounts, reassessment by URSSAF, and, where concealment is proved, criminal penalties for social-security contribution evasion; no direct strike-off risk attaches to this filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor ('commissaire aux comptes') for an SAS is triggered when two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at year-end: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding tax EUR 8,000,000; average permanent workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for companies that control or are controlled by another entity above the audit thresholds, or when requested by shareholders or the commercial court.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles (Plan Comptable Général) as codified in the Code de commerce; consolidated financial statements must comply with IFRS if the company is listed or belongs to a listed group; a simplified presentation is permissible for micro-entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a stand-alone annual UBO declaration for an unchanged SAS. The SAS must, however, continuously maintain an accurate register of beneficial owners and file any beneficial-ownership change via the INPI Guichet Unique within 30 days of the triggering event. The annual accounts filings prompt a registry cross-check of shareholding information and the beneficial-owner register; any inconsistency must be rectified immediately in the on-site statutory records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des actions et mouvements de titres (share register and transfer ledger)
Registre des procès-verbaux et décisions des associés (minute book)
Registre des conventions de l'associé unique or related-party transaction register, where applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 500–1,500 per annum (approximately USD 540–1,620) for registered-office services and annual corporate secretarial agent fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,000–12,000 per engagement (approximately USD 3,240–12,960) for a certified audit where mandatory; no audit fee should be budgeted if the SAS remains below all statutory audit thresholds and no voluntary audit is implemented

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced corporate income tax rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit per fiscal year for SMEs whose turnover is below EUR 10 million. No general statutory tax holiday applies to an ordinary French SAS. The Research Tax Credit (CIR) may provide a 30% credit on eligible R&D expenses if laser puzzle design and cutting qualify. Unused losses are carried forward indefinitely, but annual utilisation is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding that amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return) accompanied by supporting balance-sheet schedules 2050 to 2059; electronically filed through the French corporate tax e-filing system (EDI-TéléIR / TéléTVA) on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the return and annual settlement must be filed electronically by the third working day after 1 May. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the return must be filed no later than three months after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit of the fiscal year before offset of carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source net taxable income in EUR; allocate the result of the French business or permanent establishment and retain supporting transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax loss of the fiscal year available for carryforward or carryback.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SAS must report a loss only if attributable to a French taxable activity; loss utilisation follows Article 209 CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory extra-accounting restatements: non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, depreciation recapture, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same adjustments to the French branch/SAS result; disallow head-office charges unless supported by allocation and arm's-length evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of prior-year losses used in the current year, subject to the statutory cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter carried-forward French losses only; keep computation schedules showing the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% annual deduction ceiling.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late non-filing or late filing triggers a penalty of 10% of the assessed tax if no formal demand has been issued, 40% of the assessed tax after a formal notice (mise en demeure), and 80% of the assessed tax for fraudulent participation. In addition, monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% applies to the unpaid corporate income tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for distributions made to non-resident corporate shareholders; 12.8% final withholding at source for non-resident individual beneficiaries, possibly supplemented by social levies where French social-security rules apply.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty-reduced or treaty-exempt dividend treatment, the beneficial owner must submit a current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority to the French paying entity before the distribution. For EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% of the capital for an uninterrupted 24-month period, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive can eliminate the French withholding at source. If the domestic withholding was already applied, a refund claim must be filed with the French tax authorities (Service des Impôts) no later than 31 December of the second calendar year following the distribution, attaching the TRC, ownership evidence, and the relevant double-taxation-agreement analysis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory domestic withholding of 33.33% applies to sums paid by a French taxpayer to a non-resident for the use of patents, trademarks, know-how, or similar intangible rights, unless reduced or eliminated by an applicable DTA or the EU Interest & Royalties Directive; treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%. Interest: domestic law generally imposes no withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents on ordinary debt, except for payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions (ETNC) subject to a 75% withholding/anti-abuse charge; most DTAs cap interest withholding at 0% or 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Master File and Local File documentation is mandatory under Article L13 AA of the French Book of Tax Procedures for entities whose annual turnover or total balance-sheet assets equal or exceed EUR 400 million. Entities below that threshold must nevertheless provide simplified transfer-pricing documentation under Article L13 AB when related-party transactions exceed EUR 200,000 per fiscal year. Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a distinct offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime. However, a French SAS is subject to the general anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit under Article L64 LPF), the OECD BEPS Principal Purpose Test under tax treaties, and permanent-establishment/effective-management jurisprudence. A company with no physical premises, no employees, no local decision-making, and no active business in France risks being recharacterised as a sham or tax-resident elsewhere, thereby losing treaty benefits and facing reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment of taxable turnover from Amazon Pay or Stripe settlement accounts, undocumented cash sales, false invoices, fictitious expenses, or omission of French-source income from the corporate income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI, tax evasion is punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated or organised offences carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a EUR 3,000,000 fine. Administrative penalties of 80% of the omitted tax plus 0.20% monthly interest are also imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who personally participates in the evasion may be criminally convicted, subjected to a ban on managing a business (interdiction de gérer), ordered to pay restitution, and held civilly liable for the corporate tax debts through an action en comblement de passif under Article L651-2 of the French Commercial Code if the company is liquidated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an SAS with a virtual office, maintaining no French employees, making no management decisions in France, and using the French entity solely to route payments or obtain treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may be disregarded under the French abus de droit doctrine; the tax authorities can impose an 80% penalty on the reassessed tax, deny treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test, and shift the tax residence or profit allocation to the actual place of management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be pursued personally for corporate tax liabilities resulting from misuse of the legal entity, face criminal sanctions for complicity in tax evasion, and be subject to travel bans (interdiction de quitter le territoire) and prohibitions on holding managerial office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or produce the Local File/Master File, use of non-arm's-length pricing for intercompany royalty, management, or service fees, or absence of contemporaneous documentation for cross-border related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authorities may reassess profits using the arm's-length standard and impose the 5% documentation penalty under Article 1732 bis CGI on the amount of the adjustment when required documentation is not provided within 30 days of a request; interest at 0.20% per month accrues. Repeat non-cooperation can lead to an additional fine of up to EUR 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false or artificial intercompany agreements may be jointly liable for the resulting corporate tax assessment and can be criminally prosecuted for concealment where pricing manipulation is intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without applying the 25% statutory withholding or without documenting treaty relief, and processing Amazon Pay or Stripe settlements outside the corporate bank account to conceal distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company remains liable for the unpaid withholding tax, plus late-payment interest and a penalty of 5% of the unpaid withheld tax under Article 1731 CGI; in case of intentional omission, the 80% bad-faith penalty applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president of the SAS can be personally liable for failure to remit source taxes if found to have acted intentionally; criminal fines and imprisonment for fraudulent concealment of withheld taxes may be imposed, and travel bans and management bans are available.
